long_biography.plain_text:
Work came before ownership in Maneas’s career. Raised in Bondi Junction by Kytherian immigrants, he studied construction and engineering while earning money at a relative’s restaurant. A notice at university led to a cadetship; the employer expanded tenfold during his nearly two decades there. That experience gave him technical and managerial grounding for a riskier step in 1998.

Maneas and a business partner put their houses on the line to establish what became Ganellen. The venture became a substantial construction enterprise under his control, with Maneas holding most shares directly or indirectly, before the group entered external administration. More recent reporting associates him with Ganellen Property Group’s retail investments and a proposed Sydney redevelopment. Away from building sites, he conceived My Greek Odyssey to introduce audiences to overlooked islands, local histories and Greek communities. He remains its on-screen host; the official programme site records seven seasons and 77 episodes.
